_comment: Real-time timing, pacing and the live league's identity. Sport/engine values (incl. game-clock lengths) live in data/rules.json. See docs/channel.md. Times written "day N HH:MM" are wall-clock times in live.timeZone, counted from the season's Monday (day 1).

live._comment: The always-on league. Every browser rebuilds it, with season 1 starting at 00:00 on firstSeasonStarts (a Monday) in timeZone (an IANA zone follows daylight saving). mode: 'seed' plays it from seed (the dev league; ?seed= too), 'keys' from the day keys in keys/ (Task 271: the live league's seed is secret; npm run daykey makes the keys from it; docs/live.md 5). looks: a public seed for appearance only (the presenters, the managers' names, the ads' order), never results, so the desk looks the same whatever the league's seed.

match._comment: A match plays its 2 halves in realMinutes. The game clock pauses goalPauseSeconds after a goal and subPauseSeconds after a substitution (one pause per moment, the longest), and freeShotPauseSeconds between a foul and the free shot it gives (Task 67; Task 143: 6 s, staged: the referee carries the ball to the mark, the others clear to an arc, the kick), and foulPauseSeconds after any other foul (Task 144: the referee sets the ball where it was, the others reshape, a restart pass), so a match runs a little longer than that; the calendar checks leave pauseAllowanceMinutes for them.

calendar._comment: Regular-season matches play one at a time, evenly spaced from firstKickoff up to finalRoundKickoff. With finalRoundSimultaneous, the last round's matches all kick off at finalRoundKickoff.

playoffs._comment: Fixed kick-offs in play order: semifinal 1, semifinal 2, final (just the final with 2 playoff teams).

segments._comment: The slot around each live match: preMatchMinutes of pre-match card, then walkOutMinutes of walk-out up to kick-off; after the whistle, handshakeMinutes, then the post-match show (postMatchMinutes in all: the full-time card for fullTimeMinutes, player of the match for potmSeconds, this match's highlights, then studio cards). After the final, the trophy lift (trophyLift) takes the handshakes' place, and the post-match show is followed by the champions (championMinutes: 10 until Task 190, then 4, the lift having taken most of their time; 1 since Task 206, Tom: one card, the lift and the awards having shown the rest) and the off-season. studioDecks (Tom's note 11, 2026-10-19): the studio cards dealt by phase from shuffled decks (until then two fixed rotations, studioCards and afterFinalCards (Task 206), each block carrying on from where the last stopped). A studio block shows cardsPerBlock cards. raceFromGamesLeft: THE PLAYOFF RACE is dealt only once no team has more than this many regular-season games left (Task 278n).

studioDecks._comment: The studio cards by phase (Tom's note 11, 2026-10-19; docs/studio-cards.md, docs/channel.md §16.9): each studio block deals cardsPerBlock cards from its phase's deck, a seeded shuffle per gap, every card in the pool before any comes round again, a new shuffle never opening with the card the last ended on; a card with nothing to say is skipped (cards.js cardShows). Fixed slots: LATEST RESULTS first in the post-match show's block, the promo leading each block before a big match. The phases: early (the regular season's first earlyDays days), late (the rest of it), finalRound (the final round to the first semifinal), playoffs (from a semifinal to the final), afterFinal (the final to the new season). recordsWatchShare: RECORDS WATCH shows a leader with this share of a season record. rookieKeeperStarts: ROOKIES lists rookie keepers with this many starts. farewells: FAREWELLS lists at most this many. 'upcoming' becomes the bracket once the regular season is over and the new-season countdown after the final.

highlights._comment: Highlights packages of recent matches fill the gaps between live ones (after the re-airs), each opening with a sting naming the match and when it was played, then a short studio block (ads if due, segments.cardsPerBlock cards). The matches just shown in the post-match show go to the back of the queue. A package has every goal and any shootout, plus the biggest other moments (hot shots, saves, blocks, burns) up to maxClips clips in all, in match order. Each clip shows leadMs before its moment and tailMs after (on screen, real ms), played at speed (Task 278g, Tom: 1.15, was 1.5, too quick, more so on a TV; the packages keep their length, each clip showing a little less of the play before its moment). The pool is the last poolSize finished matches, newest first, cycled so each package airs several times, but no package more than perGap times in one gap (Task 206, Tom: after the channel's very first match its highlights played about 40 times running); studio blocks fill the rest. Task 213 (Tom): on the night after the final, the last round's packages give way to the playoffs' reels: one kind of moment across the semis and the final, in the order played, titled by reels (goals: every goal, golden goals included; saves: the saves off hot shots, the big ones; scorchers: every scorcher), after the semis' packages, in that order reelPasses times round, then the semis again while they fit. A reel with nothing in it is left out.

preview._comment: The PLAYOFF PREVIEW show (the big matches promoted, Tom 2026-10-17; docs/channel.md §30.1), in the long gap between the final round and the semifinals: first right after the final round's show, then again before a re-air once everyMinutes have passed since the last one began, starting no later than lastStart (in live.timeZone) on the semifinals' day. Its running order: the opening (openingSeconds), a desk clip, THE TABLE'S STORY, the playoff analyst on the four (data/analyst.json; analystSeconds at most, sized to the lines), the GOALS OF THE SEASON reel (the regular season's goals, scorchers first, seasonReelClips at most), BY THE NUMBERS (numberTiles tiles), then for each semifinal the analyst on it, TALE OF THE TAPE, the meetings reel (this season's goals between the two, meetingReelClips at most) and PLAYERS TO WATCH, then the SEMIFINALS promo card; each card cardSeconds. reels: the reels' names (the highlights' sting; the meetings reel is named by its two teams). FINALS PREVIEW (Tom, 2026-10-18; docs/channel.md §30.3), in the gap between the second semifinal and the final: right after the second semifinal's show, then again before a re-air once finalsEveryMinutes have passed since the last one began, if it ends before the final's run-in. Its running order: the opening, a desk clip (the final set), THE ROAD TO THE FINAL, a reel of both semifinals' goals (reels.semis), TALE OF THE TAPE, the finalists' meetings reel (meetingReelClips at most), PLAYERS TO WATCH, THE FINAL's promo card.

animation._comment: Match animation, in real milliseconds unless noted. Players head for their spots at runSpeed near the ball, easing to jogSpeed at nearBall or further (speeds in pitch lengths per real second, nearBall in pitch lengths), and slow into place over settleMs. After a turnover, players next to the ball react after reactNearMs and those nearBall away after reactFarMs. Long spells without events split into phases of about probeMs (fresh runs, the ball closed down harder), each later phase starting with a pass to a teammate with chance holdPassChance. passMs / shotMs: ball travel time. A pass takes longer the further it goes (Task 169): its length over passSpeed (pitch lengths per real second), never quicker than passMs (a short pass, and the ball's other quick moves) nor slower than passMaxMs; a pass to the sim's next moment sets off that much earlier, so it still arrives as the moment happens. touchChance: of the passes to a shooter, the share that arrive early (Task 170): the receiver has the ball between touchMinMs and touchMaxMs (seeded) before striking it, if the moments before leave room (otherwise it's first time). goalHoldMs: the ball rests in the net before the restart. burnFlashMs: the burn flash. kickoffHoldMs: everyone stands still this long at each kick-off. keeperTrackMs: in play, keepers move across and off their line with the ball, following where it has been over this long (so about half of it behind). runChance: at each kick-off, change of possession or advance, the chance that the outfield player on the ball sets off on a run, keeping it through every advance until the possession ends or the next shot. goalCelebrateMs: in the pause after a goal, the scorers celebrate this long, then everyone jogs to their restart spot for the rest of it. refereeTrackMs: the referee follows play on a diagonal, heading for where the ball has been over this long (so they lag it and never sprint for long). refereeSignalMs: after a goal or a foul the referee raises an arm this long. managerTrackMs: each manager paces their stretch of touchline with the ball, following where it has been over this long.
animation._ballSpin: The ball's spin (Tom, 2026-10-16, on ballspin.html: the core's dark pixel on a round ball; the edge pattern dropped, it made the ball harder to follow): it turns as it travels, perPixel of the core's steps a second for each stage pixel a second it's going (4 make a whole turn), at most maxSteps a second (a pixel ball turning faster just flickers); a jump of more than jumpMs on its clock (a replay, a skip) starts the turn afresh.
animation._shotBend: Bending shots (Tom, 2026-10-16): off for now (share 0; Tom: without the ball visibly spinning a curl looks wrong; revisit later, docs/backlog.md). When on, this share of shots curl in flight, seeded by the shot, ending where they would anyway (presentation only): a sideways bow at the middle of min to max pitch lengths, at most maxShare of the shot's length.
animation._cheers: Task 278l (Tom): celebrations that cheer. goal: after a goal the scorer and the nearest teammate (pair) or every outfielder (group) gather round the scorer and cheer on a beat, arms up with a hop (the pair high-five); none: as before (they run to a spot and stand). winners: at full time the winners cheer in their huddle and, after a home win, through the salute. ?cheer=pair|group|none on the dev server (pair and group with the winners cheering). Mock-ups on cheers.html; Tom's pick (2026-10-13): pair, and the winners cheering.
animation._momentumRing: Task 238 (Tom): when a team gains momentum (a scorcher, or the other side's burn), rings pulse out round each of its players; the scorebug swatch's glow fades with the momentum left. Task 255: pulses rings, each growing from radius 4 by reach px and fading over pulseMs, one every gapMs, width px thick (a heat-yellow core from 2); a heat-orange glow at each player's feet fading over glowMs (0: none); over: drawn over the players instead of under them. Tom's pick B on momentum.html (Task 238's was 1 pulse, 1000 ms, 1 px, reach 7).
animation._bigKickSpeed: Task 240: a keeper's big kick (a pass of 0.35 pitch lengths or more, up high) travels at this speed (pitch lengths per real second), slower than passSpeed, so it hangs in the air (0.3 at first; Tom: a touch slow).
animation._shootout: Task 277b (Tom: players should move about as each kicker sets up): the shootout staged (Tom's pick B on shootouts.html; the old standing lines removed in the clean-up, 2026-10-21). Each player keeps a spot near the centre circle (keepers by the box); the next taker walks at walkSpeed (pitch lengths per real second) to just behind the mark, stands standMs, runs up over runUpMs and strikes; the keepers take turns in goal, bouncing on the line (bounce, a share of the pitch's width, every bounceMs) and diving; the ball rolls back to the mark over returnMs; the waiting players mill about by mill (a share of the pitch's width); a team that scores puts its arms up for celebrateMs; after the last kick the winners cheer and the losers hold their heads.

poses._comment: Livelier players (Task 120; docs/channel.md §17.4), visual only: the sim and where players are don't change. Speeds are in pitch lengths per real second, read from where each player was at 100 ms marks on the match clock (sampleMs), so every screen agrees. The run: below walkSpeed both feet down; four steps (both down, left up, both down, right up), a step every stepMs[0] at walkSpeed easing to stepMs[1] at sprintSpeed and faster, sprinting kicking the free foot back and pumping the arms. The ball at the carrier's feet goes to the side they're heading once they've moved that way faster than footSpeed over footMs[0] (or footMs[1], for slow drifts); otherwise toward the goal they attack. Kicks: as a pass sets off, kickMs; a shot, shotKickMs (leaning in). A keeper's dive at a shot saved or scored: the leap from diveLeadMs before it lands for diveLeadMs + diveMs, then kneeMs on one knee. Turf kicked up (flecks): turfStride behind each sprinting step, turfTurn when a runner faster than turnSpeed changes direction or the ball changes feet, turfKick at a pass, turfShot at a shot, turfDive where a keeper lands.
poses._saves: Tom, 2026-10-20 (saves.html): not the dive every time. Each shot saved or scored picks the keeper's move by its seed: a held save a standing catch (catch of them) or the dive, a parried one a standing parry (parry) or the dive, a goal the dive or the keeper beaten barely moving (beaten). A standing save lasts as the leap does, with no knee; a save's dive or parry goes to a seeded side.

play._comment: Wide play on the pitch (Task 79; docs/channel.md §15.3), presentation only. flankChance: the chance a possession goes down a flank (the carrier in a wide lane, both teams leaning that way); wideOutletChance: the same when it starts with the keeper (played out wide). cornerChance: on a flank, as the ball reaches the attacking zone, the chance the player on the ball heads for the corner area, then crosses it back to the shooter or cuts in to shoot (kept until the next shot). switchChance: on a flank, the chance a pass in a long spell goes across to the far side and play switches flank. The soft offside (Task 80; §15.4): tether is how far (pitch lengths) an attacker off the ball may stand beyond the last outfield defender, or beyond the ball if it's further forward (never on a breakaway); lineDrop is the share of any gap beyond that closed by the last defender dropping back, the attackers checking back for the rest. Loose balls (Task 82; §15.5): every block and parried save, and a tackle that isn't a steal with chance looseTackleChance, sends the ball loose: looseReachMin–Max (pitch lengths) off a block or parry, tackleReachMin–Max off a tackle, rolling for looseMinMs–looseMaxMs (real ms, shorter if the next moment comes sooner) while the player the sim gave it to races the nearest opponent to it and gets there first. Breakaways (Task 253, Tom's pick B on breakaways.html; §22.4): the player who breaks sets off goal-ward breakaway.leadMs (real ms) before the sim's breakaway, carrying it or running onto the through ball, with no passing it about first, so the break is one burst; on the breakaway their teammates off the ball hang back at least breakaway.hang (pitch lengths) behind the ball, level with the chasing defenders, so it reads 1 on 0.

reairs._comment: Full re-airs of earlier matches fill each gap after the post-match show (labelled REPLAY, at 1x). Each: an intro card (introSeconds), the line-up (lineUpSeconds), the match with half-time cut to halfTimeSeconds, the handshakes (handshakeSeconds), a full-time card while the crowd drains (fullTimeSeconds), the recorded interview (interviewSeconds), then a studio block (docs/channel.md §16.3). After a regular match at play position k, the re-airs are the matches at k - offsets, newest first; after the final round, a knockout or the final, they cycle through the last poolSize (between the second semifinal and the final, the two semifinals alone, Tom 2026-10-18) matches. A re-air only starts if its whole unit ends before the run-in.
reairs._finalCelebrateSeconds: Task 278f (Tom, A): a final re-aired in a gap ends with the champions celebrating by their fans (the trophy lift's start, as it aired) in the handshakes' place, this long, and the celebration carries on behind the full-time card; the whole lift still re-airs on the night after the final.

studio._comment: The talk at the desk between matches (docs/channel.md §16.2, §16.4, §16.7). In the post-match show: the match talk (matchTalkSeconds; roundTalkSeconds in the simultaneous final round), the interview's tee-up (interviewTeeUpSeconds), then after the interview the wrap-up (wrapUpSeconds). In studio blocks: a clip on something else (clipSeconds), its kind from clipKinds in a seeded order, never the same twice running; the last block of a gap only gets one if it's at least minBlockForTalkSeconds long. Before every live match the tee-up talk (teeUpSeconds). After the final, the off-season opens with a talk (offseasonTalkSeconds) inside its own length (the champions' talk went, Tom after Task 258: the match talk crowns them, then the final's highlights and the champions' cards); after the moves board the desk signs off (signoffTalkSeconds, Task 194): the season done, the new one's opener. On the desk (Task 98) the one talking makes their line's gesture for its first gestureSeconds, then just talks; the other nods now and then (every third nodEverySeconds). In the player-of-the-match interview (Task 100) the player listens to the unheard question, nodding, for interviewQuoteDelaySeconds before their quote types out (at captions.quoteCharsPerSecond). Task 187 (the desk's pauses): every talk length above (and opening.talkSeconds, segments.potmSeconds, reairs.interviewSeconds) is now the most it can run; each talk runs only as long as its lines: the first starts lineLeadSeconds in (after the studio jingle where it plays), each runs for its clip (assets/voices/lengths.json) and stays up lineHoldSeconds more, lineGapSeconds before the next, the talk ending talkTailSeconds after its last line. A line's graphic under the desk outlasts it (Tom): up until the next graphic or the talk's end, and for at least showMinSeconds (longer ones at showCharsPerSecond), so a line with a graphic waits for the one before's to be read, and the talk for its last. The interview runs the nod, the quote's clip and interviewHoldSeconds to read the caption bar. Task 247a: a quote in two parts (a reaction, then a fact) plays them back to back, interviewPartGapSeconds apart. The time saved goes to the cards (the post-match show keeps its length).

ads._comment: In-universe ad breaks (docs/channel.md §16.11): a bumper in, perBreak ads of adSeconds, a bumper out (bumperSeconds each). One opens a studio block when the last break ended at least minGapMinutes earlier in the slot (the post-match show's block always has one); never in a match, a highlights package, a re-air or the run-in. The playoffs promo (Task 111) is only in the order from promoFromShare of the way through the regular season (by kick-offs) until the first semifinal kicks off, then as the final's promo (with the finalists once both semifinals have finished) until the final kicks off; outside that the breaks carry on with the other ads. In Full, during match pictures, the strip above the ground shows one ad as a still (Task 113), the next every stillMinutes of the league's clock, each ad once a pass in a fresh seeded order (Task 158; the promo only in its window). The night after the off-season show (Task 195, Tom) ends on a run of ads up to the new season's run-in: the whole slate (less the playoffs promo) closingSlates times, in an order of its own. Between two ads in a break, a darker pixel dissolve over the new ad's first dissolveMs (Task 118): the old ad breaks up into near-black cell by cell, the new one appears out of it.

transitions._comment: Transitions between pictures (docs/channel.md §16.10), worked out from segment edges so no times move: the glass sweep into and out of the scene (sceneMs, over the stadium's side of the edge; its glass band glassPx wide), the diagonal band between highlight clips (clipStingMs, centred on the cut) and opening each package (coming down half a clip sting before it, holding on the match's name, lifting openStingSeconds after it starts), and between the desk and the interview (cutMs). One studio card to the next over the scene: a soft dissolve (cardDissolveMs, Tom after Task 101). A card over the pitch (pre-match, full time, a re-air's) fades in over cardFadeMs, settling up into place, and the pre-match card fades out as the walk-out begins (Task 278k, Tom's pick A: they cut in; the others leave with the sweep into the studio).

scene._comment: The scene between matches (Task 96; docs/channel.md §16.1): the light bars. The backdrop in bands steps; slope: how far right each row down is shifted (a diagonal); bars: each bar's width (stage px), speed (px a second), starting offset and opacity; an orange line at lineAt of the height with a bright run of runPx along it at runPxPerSecond; sparkles twinkling pixels. Colours are in palette.js.

opening._comment: The channel's opening, once a day (docs/channel.md §16.5a): the ident (identSeconds), then the presenters' welcome (talkSeconds), right before the tee-up of the first live match from at (wall-clock, live.timeZone), and before each season's first match. After the final's night, a new season's countdown (countdownSeconds, Task 277b) between the closing ads and the ident.

ceremonies._comment: Walk-out, half-time and handshakes (real time; speeds are animation.jogSpeed). Walk-out: players walk on from the tunnel in pairs (one from each team, Task 63), walkOnGapMs apart, and line up (walkOnSeconds), the home then away anthem (anthemSeconds each), a warm-up (warmUpSeconds, a new spot every warmUpMoveSeconds), then breakLineSeconds before kick-off they jog to their kick-off spots. At half-time and before overtime, outfield players gather by their bench and keepers change ends; breakLineSeconds before the restart everyone heads for their spot. Substitutes follow the starters out to their dugouts. Handshakes (whole squads, substitutes too): handshakeParts are fractions of the whole: each team huddling just off its end of the lines, the players peeling off into their line and walking along it past every opponent (at handshakeLineSpeed, pitch lengths per real second, or quicker if a short re-air needs it), the home salute (after a home win) or going to the benches; the rest is walking off down the tunnel, in pairs. Each opposing pair meeting in the procession is a beat where everyone holds for handshakePauseMs (Task 74). Without a home win there's no salute: both teams go straight off and the handshakes are shorter. The tunnel's gate (Task 63) opens and shuts over gateMs: open for the walk-out (until the teams head for their kick-off spots), the breaks and the handshakes, shut during play.
ceremonies._saluteCheer: Tom (2026-10-16): the home end cheering the home team's salute after a home win, as it cheers a home goal (a run of overlapping roars, each a little smaller, crowd.js GOAL_CHEER), at this power; no chant or applause (Tom).

awards._comment: The awards on air (Task 191, Tom's pick B on offseason.html), after the champions: the desk's intro (talkSeconds at most, sized to its lines like any talk), then each award for awardSeconds on the plinth over the scene, in this order (the sim's ids, data/rules.json awards; the Ember Boot last). An award the sim didn't give is left out. Each: the prize on its plinth, the two runners-up named on the card in turn (third at shortlistAt, second at secondAt), the winner stepping in at winnerAt and lifting it at liftAt; the rest of the time they hold it up.

farewells._comment: The farewells (Task 192, Tom's pick C on offseason.html), after the awards: the season's notable retirements as a gallery of framed portraits over the scene, each lit in turn for perPlayerSeconds with their card. Notable (Tom: long careers and awards): retired from a team, ranked by seasons played with each award won counting awardWeight seasons more, up to max. Inside the off-season's own length (segments.offseasonSummaryMinutes).

lottery._comment: The draft lottery (Task 192, Tom's pick A on offseason.html, the tumbler), after the farewells: the odds for oddsSeconds, then each pick drawn for revealSeconds, the last pick first so the No. 1 comes last: the drum spins up, the ball drops at dropAt and lands in the tray, filling its row on the board. The sim has already drawn it (the draft_lottery event). Inside the off-season's own length.
lottery._sound: Task 204, Tom's pick A on the sound board: each draw's sound (musicRecipes.js lotteryLayers): the balls rattling as the drum spins up, the drop down the chute, a clunk into the tray, a bell (levels.lottery). The music carries on softly under it (sound.music.lotteryLevel).

draft._comment: The draft on air (Task 193, Tom's pick on offseason.html: the board, then the close-up), after the lottery: each round 1 pick for round1Seconds: the board with the pick on the clock, from walkAt the pick walking up in the board's window, at cutAt a cut to the close-up, the shirt fading on and the card coming in together from kitAt (Task 198, Tom: a moment after the cut; no ratings on the card: what they're projected to be), a fist-pump from cheerAt. Round 2 on the board only, round2Seconds a pick, the name up at round2NameAt with the card below. Inside the off-season's own length.

moves._comment: The moves board on air (Task 194, Tom's pick B on offseason.html), after the draft: the off-season's free-agent signings, then the veteran releases, then the Kindling League's call-ups (Tom's order; not the draft's own picks or reserves whose rights ran out), up to maxLines, perPage lines to a page of the board. leadSeconds before the first line, then each line lineSeconds (its letters flapping in, its player's card from cardAt into its turn), then tailSeconds; at least minSeconds. Then the desk signs off (studio.signoffTalkSeconds). Inside the off-season's own length.

trophyLift._comment: After the final (Task 190, Tom's pick B on offseason.html), in place of the handshakes, before the post-match show: the champions celebrate by their fans (celebrateSeconds) while the runners-up stand about; the runners-up form a guard of honour and the champions file along it, shaking hands (guardSeconds); the champions' anthem, the squad lined up across halfway (anthemSeconds; their own tune, as at the walk-out); then the lift (liftSeconds): a podium on the centre circle in the wide shot, the champions climbing onto it, then after closeUpAfterSeconds a cut to the close-up of the five who started the final, the captain (their best outfield starter) lifting the Scorch Cup, confetti. The crowd stays: the champions' fans until near the end, the runners-up's thinning.
trophyLift._stageAfterSeconds: Tom (2026-10-20, his pick C on offseason.html): this long into the close-up, a flash and a cut back wide to a stage where the podium stood, an arch in the champions' colours over it, the cup passed down the line from the captain, fireworks over the stands, to the end of the lift.

captions._comment: How long lower-third captions stay on screen, in real milliseconds. Goals stay longer. alertMs: goal alerts from other live matches (final round). calloutMs: the on-pitch speech bubbles (TACKLE!, SAVE!, FOUL! …). subCalloutMs: the SUB ON bubble over a player coming on, shown alongside them. quoteCharsPerSecond: how fast the player of the match's quote types out in its speech bubble. recordMs (Task 220b): a record falling has the caption bar to itself this long, after the goal's caption when it's a goal or an assist.

updates._comment: How an update reaches viewers (Task 274; docs/live.md 3): the channel checks version.json (written by npm run publish) every checkSeconds; a new version reloads a hidden or silent channel by itself and shows UPDATE READY over one playing sound.

switches._comment: Changes published early and switched on at a moment (Task 274; docs/live.md 3): a name and its time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in the league's time zone; the code asks switchedOn(config, name, t) (src/channel/updates.js). None yet.

ticker._comment: The bottom crawl. pxPerSecond is in stage pixels. results / upcoming: how many of each to show. goalFlashMs: how long a live score flashes after a goal. announcementHours (Task 265, docs/channel.md §24): how long a League announcement leads the crawl after it airs (it stays in INFO's UPDATES for good).

table._comment: The league table panel. slideMs: how long a row takes to glide to its new place when the order changes (real milliseconds).

kits._comment: If two teams' primary colours are closer than this (RGB distance, 0-442), the away team wears its secondary colour.

replays._comment: Instant goal replays (Task 57): during a goal's pause, delayMs after the goal (real milliseconds), a small inset replays the match from leadMs before the goal to tailMs after it, magnified zoom times, played at speed (below 1: slowed), the camera following the ball averaged over followMs either side (Task 71, Tom's pick F); w and h are the inset's size in stage pixels. It only shows if it ends inside the pause.

broadcast._comment: Broadcast mode (Task 55): the ground (everything drawn on the pitch canvas) moves right by shiftPx (43 centres it, leaving a stand on each side), sliding over slideMs (real milliseconds) while the stands and panels fade across.
broadcast._peekMs: Task 278d (Tom: for immersion, and against screen burn-in): in Broadcast the scorebug (with its layout and sound controls) fades away for each ad break and the opening (the new season's countdown, the ident) and back after, never during a transition; a mouse moving over the picture brings it back for peekMs (real ms).
broadcast._awayEnd: The away end by the match (Tom, 2026-10-16; stands.js awayCorner, awaySteps): a step bigger when the two teams share a region, and a step when the away team tops the table (once it has played leaderAfterPlayed); each step spreads it leftPx further along the top stand and downPx further down the right-hand stand, stage px.

clips._comment: The clip tool (clips.html, npm run clip; getting the word out, docs/launch-plan.md): moments worth a clip from what has aired, each recorded from leadSeconds before its moment to tailSeconds after (by kind: a goal, a golden goal, a shootout's deciding kick); listMax the most listed, the best first. Dev tool only, never on air.

podcast._comment: OFF THE BALL, the podcast (docs/podcast.md; podcastTalk.js): each regular-season day's episode is made at `at` (live.timeZone), from what has aired by then, and its repeats say the same; SEASON AHEAD (day 1) too, SEASON REVIEW once the final has finished. Each daily episode airs at the first break from `at` (a re-air giving way when it doesn't fit) and again from repeatAt the next night, except in PLAYOFF PREVIEW's gap; SEASON REVIEW at the start of the night after the final and again before its repeats. An episode (Tom, 2026-10-20: a major event, about 9-10 minutes) has `discussions` of them, and the day's goals as a reel of reelClips at most (scorchers first). A new topic waits topicBeatSeconds before its first line (Tom, 2026-10-21), and the booth's screen wipes to a new graphic over wipeMs. PICKS: the biggest match (the two sides' points together) kicking off within pickHours after it, judged by the next episode. Interjections (off, interjectionShare 0: Tom, 2026-10-21, they sounded like a bug; voiced, kept): the listener's, under the other's line when it's at least interjectionChars long, interjectionShare of the time (seeded), a little under halfway through it, at interjectionLevel of the voices' level. The studio jingle opens each airing. The premiere is promoted for promoHours before it: the poster card leading every studio block, an item on the ticker.

vault._comment: FROM THE VAULT (Tom's note 14; picked on vault.html; docs/channel.md §33; vault.js): a package on one big match from the past (for now last season's final), from fromSeason on, about each time in `at` (live.timeZone): the gap that holds the time airs it at the first break from it (sooner if a re-air would carry it past the run-in), if it fits; never between the second semifinal and the final, nor on the night after the final. Its running order: the opening card (openSeconds), the match's reel (as a highlights package), SINCE THEN (sinceSeconds), then a studio block. on: false leaves it out.

groundsTour._comment: AROUND THE GROUNDS (Tom's note 14; picked on groundstour.html; docs/channel.md §32; groundsTour.js, groundScenes.js): a tour of every ground with no match on, visitSeconds at each, something going on there (five training scenes, five for the groundstaff, dealt so none repeats; only the groundstaff at night, when the light is past halfway from dusk to night, nightLevel, and on the night after the final). One per gap, after the first re-air (or in place of the re-airs when none fits), and on the night after the final among its filler; never between the second semifinal and the final (note 16). Each ground wipes in over the last: a band wipeWidth of the picture wide in the new club's colours, over wipeMs. fans: how full the stands are for training and for the groundstaff (0–1). on: false leaves it out.

lighting._comment: The light by the time of day on the league's clock (live.timeZone; Tom's note 14, picked on groundstour.html; docs/channel.md §31; lighting.js): day from dayFrom, dusk from duskFrom, night from nightFrom, dusk again (dawn) from dawnFrom, easing from one to the next over easeMinutes centred on each change. At dusk and night the picture is multiplied by a tint (around: the stands and the dark round the ground, Broadcast only; ground: the ground itself, its turf below the boards, and in Full the turf down to the ticker), eased toward no tint by strength (Tom: 0.5); pool: the strongest of the floodlights' four pools of light on the ground (before strength); glow: round each lamp (Broadcast). The floodlights stand on their mounts in Broadcast's stands' corners all day, lit from dusk. The studio, the scene, the ads and the cards are never lit. on: false leaves every picture as it was.

crowd._comment: How loud the crowd's murmur is (0-1, before sound.levels.crowd), Task 52. base: play in midfield. attack: added as the ball reaches the goal a home attack is going for (awayAttack: the share of that an away attack gets, since the crowd is mostly home fans). heat: added at full heat. breakaway: added during a breakaway. bigStage: added in the final round and the playoffs. reair: re-airs are this much as loud. breaks: half-time, before overtime and during substitutions. ceremony: the walk-out and the handshakes. At each stoppage (a goal, a substitution, a miss, a held save, a foul, a burn) the murmur drops to dipLevel of itself, stays there through any pause and dipHoldSeconds into the next play, then comes back over dipReturnSeconds, so it isn't always on (Tom, 2026-10-04); dipLevel is high enough that it never sounds silent (Task 60). Quiet spells (Task 60): once no crowd reaction (roar, groan, ooh, applause, jeer) has come for quietAfterSeconds, the murmur eases down to quietLevel of itself over quietFadeSeconds, then comes back over quietReturnSeconds from the next reaction. The stands' fans follow the same share (they bob less while it's quiet).

fill._comment: How full the stands are through the hour (Task 84; docs/channel.md §15.7), 0-1 of each end. Fans arrive through the pre-match (preMatchFrom to preMatchTo) and are all in walkOutFull of the way through the walk-out (by the anthems). Full through the match, half-time and the handshakes. Then they drift away from the final whistle (Task 89, Tom: all gone before the show moves on): through the handshakes the losing side's fans to handshakeLosers and the others to handshakeOthers (after a draw, both halfway between), then through the full-time card to nobody, the losers' end empty losersGoneAt of the way through it; empty from player of the match on, for studio cards, champions and the off-season. fadeMs (real ms): each fan arriving or leaving fades in or out over this long, like a time-lapse. Highlights show their match's full crowd. A re-air fills over its intro (to reairIntro) and line-up, and empties over its handshakes.

sound._comment: Synthesized sound (Task 50; docs/channel.md §14.2). master: overall volume, 0-1. levels: each sound's loudness, 0-1, before the master: the cues (whistle, kick, shot, net, save, post, block, burn, sub) and the crowd's reactions (roar, groan, ooh, applause, jeer), each team's anthem in the walk-out, the channel's stings (post-match show, highlights, re-airs), the murmur (a small roar, played quietly and overlapping all through play), the crowd's olé chant, the transitions (Task 97): the whoosh of the glass sweep and the swish of the diagonal band, and each ad's jingle as its brand comes up (Task 105) and the studio's jingle as it returns (Task 137); the opening ident: a whoosh as the comet comes in, then a bright chord and a crackle as it lands as the O (Task 106); fire: the ident's fire following the comet round the name, identFire its style (crackle, torch or comet; Task 249); the commentator's voice (Task 123, recorded clips, see commentary); speech: the desk's and the interview's voices (Task 135); music: the off-season's loop, lottery: the draft lottery's draws, effect: the ads' small sounds (Task 203). Tune them on the sound board, sounds.html.
sound._prerender: Task 278b (Tom: every sound stuttered on his phone, a OnePlus 10 Pro, in Firefox and Chrome): every sound is built live from oscillators, noise and filters, and the crowd's need 130-200 nodes each (the murmur, three at once all through play, 500-600), the music about 800 a pass; a phone can't run them in real time. A sound needing minNodes or more is rendered once in the background (an OfflineAudioContext, the same graph) and played as a recording, kept up to cacheMB, the oldest dropped first; it plays when ready, joining part-way if that took a moment. The crowd's sounds, a new seed every cheer, are played from variants takes per kind, a roar in roarSizes sizes (its power rounded to thirds), every take rendered as sound is switched on, the crowd first, at crowdRate samples a second (half the work and memory; the crowd is low and mid tones); a crowd reaction ready more than lateSeconds late is skipped (Tom, on a smart TV: joined part-way, late ones played only their quiet tails); the rest (the music, the anthems, the ident, the lottery) exactly as before. latency: the AudioContext's latencyHint ('playback': a larger buffer, fewer dropouts, a fraction of a second later, unnoticed on a broadcast).
sound._ahead: Phones (Tom, 2026-10-13): every sound and voice starts this many seconds after it's asked for, on the audio clock. In Firefox on a phone, a sound started at the clock's 'now' lost its loud start, so passes were almost inaudible; 0.1 brought them up (0.2 little different). ?ahead= tries another on the live site too.
sound._promptSeconds: Tom, 2026-10-14: the nudge to turn sound on (CLICK FOR SOUND, the phone's pulsing SOUND) gives up after this many seconds of the channel showing without sound, not counting while the tour is open or the tab hidden: a viewer who hasn't turned it on by then wants it off (he'd been turning sound on and off to stop the nudge).
sound._recordings: Phones (Tom, 2026-10-13; vision §12): every synthesized sound recorded ahead into assets/sounds/ (recordings.html renders them in the browser from the recipes, npm run recordings compresses them; src/channel/recordings.js), so the channel only plays files: building them in the browser made the crowd and the music chop on a phone (Firefox), and Firefox played short sounds too softly. A sound that varies by its seed plays one of variants takes (the crowd crowdVariants, a roar in roarSizes sizes), picked by its seed, alike on every screen; a kick at one of kickLevels strengths, a shot at the nearest of shotPowers. rate: samples a second (the crowd crowdRate); bitrate: kbps, mono. enabled false (or ?recordings=off) builds every sound in the browser as before (prerender).

resume._comment: Task 181. After a jump (switching matches in the final round, coming back to the tab, loading mid-match, turning sound on), the sounds under way join part-way: each swells in over fadeInMs (they came in at full strength at once), the crowd's (a goal's cheer, boos, applause) at crowd times their loudness (switching into a final-round match as its home team scored peaked very loud). hiddenFadeMs: a hidden tab goes quiet, fading out over this, and fades back in when shown (its frames are slowed or stopped, so sounds came out together in bursts). switchLevel, switchReturnMs: switching to another match in the final round, everything but the voices drops to switchLevel and comes back over switchReturnMs (Tom: a home goal's cheer on the feed switched to still sounded too loud; the murmur and the cheer's later roars came in at full). hush (Tom, still a spike: to find which sound it is): on a switch, the crowd's roars (roar), the murmur (murmur), both or none go silent for hushHoldMs, then fade in over hushFadeMs; ?hush= in the URL overrides it for listening (roar, murmur, both, none). Tom listened: it was the roars, so roar.

music._comment: The off-season's music (Task 204, Tom's pick D: pulse, musicRecipes.js): it loops under the off-season's scenes (the awards, the farewells, the draft, the moves; in the repeats too), each unbroken run of them starting the loop from its top, the same on every screen; it fades out (fadeOutMs) whenever the desk talks and for the trophy lift and the champions' cards, and fades in (fadeInMs) as the next run starts. Under the lottery it carries on softly (lotteryLevel of its loudness; Tom changed his mind: it was out), so the farewells, the lottery and the draft are one run. Task 211 (Tom): it also plays under every run of studio cards, between matches all season and after the off-season, starting studioLeadSeconds into the run (after the studio jingle); the desk, ads, packages and re-airs fade it out. Under Sound in the levels pane (no slider of its own, Tom); its loudness is levels.music. Tom (after Task 258, a strange sound as it started at the cut into the awards): each run's loop starts preRollSeconds early, silent, timed to reach its top as the run begins, and is brought up over fadeInMs then, so nothing starts at the cut.
music._tracks: Task 278h (Tom: the same riff over and over): the tracks each run of music takes in turn, run by run (the studio cards' and the off-season's alike), the same on every screen: pulse (Tom's pick D, Task 204) and two of its variations on the sound board, D2 (new chords) and D3 (a new hook, running plucks); D4 (half-time) dropped (Tom: it sounded like pulse played at half speed).

commentary._comment: Tackles and steals (Task 149): one within turnoverGapSeconds of the last is never called (the first always comes, unless it is crowded). Holding the ball: one call when the picture shows one outfield player on the ball holdSeconds without a pass. Commentary (Task 123; docs/channel.md §18.2; the commentators and lines are in data/commentary.json). delayMs: a call starts this long after its moment (real ms of match playback). afterWhistleMs: kick-offs, half-time and full time are called this long after their whistle (Task 130). passRun: passes in a row by one team, as the picture draws them, before 'Nice pass.' and the like (4, Tom: 6 was too rare). minGapSeconds: at least this long between calls (a goal still comes, and drops a call just before it; chances in data/commentary.json only apply to moments that close together). followGapSeconds: a breakaway's one-two (Task 125): the shot's outcome is always called, at least this long after the call before it. goalLevels: goals (and scorchers) are this loud instead of sound.levels.commentary, to be heard over the cheering (home louder: the home end cheers more). While the voice speaks, every other sound dips to duckLevel of itself, fading over duckFadeMs each way. Its loudness is sound.levels.commentary. breathMs (Task 179): a commentator never talks over themselves: a call starts at least this long after the clip before it ends (a breakaway's one-two, a whistle wait for it; passes in a row and holding the ball are dropped instead).

chronicle._comment: The chronicle on screen (It remembers, docs/channel.md §20). The live league's chronicle takes each event once it has aired (Task 219): a match at its final whistle on screen; the awards and the off-season (retirements, the draft, moves) offseasonAiredMinutes after the final's kick-off, once the off-season show has aired them (Task 220: the final at 20:00, the show signed off by about 20:54; tests/chronicle.test.js checks the sign-off ends by then). 65 since the final's highlights came before the champions' cards (Tom, after Task 258): the sign-off about 20:53–20:57, a long final later. LATEST keeps the off-season's lines, leading, until latestOffseasonDays into the new season (Tom: the first match is at 00:30 Monday; they stay through Monday).
chronicle._search: FIND A PLAYER at the CHRONICLE's foot (Tom, 2026-10-27; docs/channel.md §20): names containing what's typed, once it's minLetters long (Tom: 3, so a letter or two never lists most of the league), the most-played first, shown at most, then and N more.

audience._comment: The AUDIENCE pane (It responds, Task 260; docs/channel.md §23): where votes and notes are sent. endpoint: the dev server's /api/audience until the launch, then the hosted service's address (vision §8; docs/live.md). noteMaxChars: the longest note a viewer can send (Task 261). noteCooldownSeconds: the least time between two notes from one browser (Task 261; the service adds its own rate limit at the launch). service: the hosted service (Task 276: a Cloudflare Worker on the live site, worker/audience.js), where the Director's desk reads the votes and notes from, with AUDIENCE_TOKEN in .env; the endpoint stays relative, so the live site's own /api/audience is the service. helloMinutes (Task 277e): the channel says hello as it starts and this often while it's showing, to count viewers (anonymously: a salted hash of the connection, and a random id for the visit); watchingMinutes: on the desk, a viewer heard from within this long is watching now.
audience._watchingTicker: Tom (2026-10-16): how many are watching as the ticker's last item, N FANS WATCHING (households heard from within watchingMinutes, asked for with each hello); off until enough people watch, ?watching=on to see it (allowed on the live site).
audience._donateUrl: Donations (Tom, 2026-10-18; docs/channel.md §23.5): the Ko-fi page linked from SUPPORT THE CHANNEL on top of FEEDBACK, a plain link out in a new tab (nothing loaded from Ko-fi; https only, checked in src/config.js).

moments._comment: MOMENTS (Milestone 5¾; docs/channel.md §25; the kinds and steps in data/moments.json). noticeSeconds: how long a notice shows below the scorebug (its entrance included); noticeGapSeconds: the pause between two notices in a queue. frameGapSeconds: a longer gap between frames (a hidden tab, a sleeping laptop) means the viewer wasn't watching: what played in it isn't counted, and a whole match in progress is broken. startGraceSeconds: a whole match needs watching from within this long after kick-off. pieceGraceSeconds: an interview or an ad break (each counted at its end, Tom) needs watching from within this long after it starts. placesSeconds: how often SEEN IT ALL looks at what's open. storageKey: where the browser keeps them (localStorage).

fanCoins._comment: Fan Coins (vision §8; docs/channel.md §29, version 2 §29.6): earned by watching, banked with the audience service, every spend shared (shared, below). enabled: false hides it all (a kill switch; on at the launch, Tom 2026-10-17). Earned while the tab shows (a gap between frames over frameGapSeconds counts nothing): a coin every liveMinutes of a live match; every offseasonMinutes of the off-season show as it airs (the lift, champions, awards, farewells, lottery, draft, moves; its repeats are replays); one a highlights package watched whole (from within graceSeconds of its start); every studioMinutes of everything else (re-airs, the desk, cards, the build-up, ads, the ident, the countdown; Tom, 2026-10-16). At most dailyCap a day, from midnight in the viewer's own time. prices: each spend's cost. A ticker message on the ticker for tickerMinutes, one after another; FAN BOARD (the back screen until Tom moved it, 2026-10-21) beside the scorebug in Full for screenMinutes, one board after another, never in the final round; a chant or a flag in a live match for the rest of the half, one per end at a time, the chant coming round every chantEverySeconds; a fan shout (Tom's notes, task 3) shoutSeconds over its end's fans, in a live match. plusSeconds: how long a +1 rises from the Audience button.

shared._comment: Version 2 (Tom, 2026-10-17; docs/channel.md §29.6): spends seen by everyone, coins banked with the audience service. queueMax: how many may wait in one queue (the ticker, FAN BOARD, a match end's shouts, a match end's chants and flags), besides the one showing. The channel checks in every checkInSeconds (banking what it earned) and reads the feed every feedSeconds; the service keeps the feed feedCacheSeconds. A spend in a match is taken only from its kick-off to matchWindowMinutes after (the longest a live match runs, overtime and a shootout too). A wallet banks at most a coin a minute, with at most bankMinutes of watching unbanked at once. noticeSeconds: when one's own spend starts, the bar under the scorebug shows this long (in Full; Tom's pick b). afterSlideSeconds (Tom, 2026-10-18): a spend in the stands that starts at once (no queue) switches to Broadcast, and for the spender starts this long after the slide is done, so its first round is seen. requestSeconds (2026-10-18): the channel gives up on a call to the service (a check-in, the feed, a spend) after this long, so one that never answers can't hold up the next. replayCacheHours (2026-10-18): a finished match's spends, which the channel shows again on its re-airs, never change, so the service lets them be kept this long.
